doubts.claim_under_doubt: adding a new runtime-required vendored JSON under server/src/vendor, wired only through copy-assets.mjs, is safely covered by the existing build/publish pipeline
doubts.fix: Extended server/src/test/build-assets.test.ts with two new assertions (dist/vendor/leadwright/claim-record-lock-contract.json exists post-build; its content is faithful to src/vendor/leadwright/) plus a beforeAll rmSync of dist/vendor so the test proves the copy step re-creates it, and corrected the file's stale docstring that only mentioned default-actions.json.
doubts.deferred_with_reason: The reviewer's other two sub-fixes — a publish-npm.yml pre-publish check for dist/vendor, and making bootstrapper/build-package.mjs's ensureBuilt re-run the build instead of trusting mere dist/ existence — touch the npm publish workflow and the bootstrapper build script, both unrelated systems with their own risk surface outside this iterate's scope (a lock-contract-explicitness change). The build-assets.test.ts fix already closes the loop for this repo's own `npm run build`, which is what every CI/publish path actually invokes; the residual gap (a stale local dist/ being reused by a manual bootstrapper run) is a pre-existing property of build-package.mjs's ensureBuilt, not something this change introduces or worsens. Recommend a follow-up iterate scoped to hardening the publish pipeline's asset-completeness checks generally, rather than folding it into this one.
